BiblicalUsage: Rabah is to increase, to multiply, to grow many. It is God's first blessing on living things — 'be fruitful, and multiply' — and His promise to Abraham, 'I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven.' Israel multiplied in Egypt until the land was filled with them, and God promised to bless and multiply His people in the land He would give them.
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that increase is God's own work: He multiplies His people, His blessing, and His praise, and the numbers are His doing, not ours. And I hold that the same word warns me — sin multiplies too, and sorrows multiply for those who hasten after another god — so I ask God to multiply what is good and to cut short what is not.
